author: nonretail_writer
central_thesis: February opens on an earnings-led relief rally that has to outrun a bear-flattening, March-lift-off Treasury curve (2Y 1.18%, 10Y 1.81%, 10Y-2Y +63 bps, 2Y +40 bps over 20 observations): investors reward credible forward growth and cash returns (Alphabet's record quarter and split, AMD's 2022 outlook, Exxon's record profit and buyback) and punish guidance or payout cuts (PayPal, AT&T), while a Russia–Ukraine energy, grain and fertiliser premium keeps an inflation floor under yields even as European gas eases, China eases policy into the Lunar New Year, and Poland's rate-hike cycle collides with its tax-cut anti-inflation shield.
sources_policy: Evidence is limited to the 2022-02-02 frozen feed (tools/digest.py) and the 2022-02-02 market card (tools/showcard.py); no other date's feed, card, spec, draft or note and no web access were used, and exclusions/2022-02-02.json lists no IDs. Every number is either a card value quoted exactly with its session tag (Yahoo Finance prior close 2022-02-01 for US/European/Japanese/Australian/Polish sessions, 2022-01-31 for the Hang Seng, 2022-01-28 for Shanghai and Korea, prior completed daily close 2022-02-01 for crypto, US Treasury prior close 2022-02-01 for yields, reference closes tagged with their own session dates) or appears in a headline cited in the same part. 265 distinct IDs are cited, none more than twice. No numeric spot-FX is used; DXY is the only dollar level quoted, and currency direction comes only from dated reporting (n0050, n1413, n1644, n1255). Previews (n0752 Amazon, n1053 S&P Global, n1156 Bank of England, n1983 January jobs report) are used only for pending events; results cited are completed before 00:00 UTC on 2022-02-02, including the Alphabet, AMD, PayPal, Starbucks and EA after-hours releases of February 1. Process note: during the survey a shared scratch file was overwritten by another process and one search output displayed eight later-dated rows from another edition; none of them was used, and all evidence was re-pulled from the own-date tools into a private directory before drafting. Verifier: tools/verify.py --nonretail 2022-02-02 PASS, 8,914 body words, 0 fail, 0 warn.
known_ambiguities_omitted: n0054 (RBA, '1 February 2022 | Minutes of the Monetary Policy Meeting'): minutes of the 1 February meeting are released two weeks later, so the item is misdated/after the cutoff; not used.
n0053 (ABC, 'Interest rates will go up', 'people need buffers' warns Reserve Bank boss): may report Governor Lowe's 2 February address, which falls after the cutoff; not used.
RBA end of bond purchases on 1 February: no own-date headline states it; the AU block cites only the February decision statement (n0065) and does not assert the end of QE.
n1106 (Tom's Hardware, 'AMD's 2022 Sales Hit $21.5 Billion'): presents a 2022 outlook as completed sales; not used. AMD's outlook is cited only via n0744.

n2050 (Reuters, Fed's Bullard sees three successive hikes): US item stamped 2022-02-01 08:00 whose publication hour is not established and could fall in the US evening after the cutoff; replaced with n1908 (Reuters poll) and n2046 (Marketplace).
Reuters LIVE MARKETS rolling pages n1230, n1209, n1161, n1807: live blogs, not used.

Numeric spot-FX items n1603 (dollar above 4 zl on 31 January) and n1590: not used; n1213 (TorFX) is cited only for the German inflation drop, and n1255/n1644/n0050/n1413 only for non-numeric currency direction.

Misdated or later-dated pages: n0757 (Bitcoin price predictions for 2025), n0931 (fake crypto websites 2023), n0452 (stocks to research in 2026), n1024/n1025 (ESPN 2026 rankings), n1971/n0586 (National Today 2027), n0633 (eToro CEG analyst target before Constellation's listing): not used.

Promotional, sensational or quote-page items: n0589 ('Expert Warns of 41% Drop'), n0098 (ig.com Uber preview), n1984 (Gold Price preview), n0873 (CRDO chart page), n1671 (Stooq WIG140 quote page), n1639 (Newseria GPW b-roll): not used.
n0010 (The Conversation, 'Inflation hits 3.5%...'): stamped before the Australian CPI release time, so misdated; AFR n0012 is used instead.
n0783/n0784 (Tesla stock jumps 11%): describes the 31 January session; not used, to avoid confusion with the card's 1 February move.
n1628 (Biznes Alert, Sierra Gorda 'new cooperative'): meaning of the headline is unclear; not used for KGHM.

Pending events without a dated own-date preview (Meta Platforms (FB), Qualcomm and Spotify results; euro-area January flash CPI; US January ADP; the OPEC+ meeting; the ECB decision): Meta and Spotify appear only as 'the next print' without dates; Qualcomm, ADP, euro-area CPI, OPEC+ and the ECB meeting date are not discussed as calendar items.

Same-day Asian releases (Australian 11:30 AEDT, Chinese 09:30 CST on 2 February) fall after the cutoff and are not used; mainland China, Hong Kong and Korea are on holiday, so their last sessions (2022-01-28 and 2022-01-31) are quoted as stale with their own dates.
n1413 (Investing.com/Reuters, dollar's biggest weekly rise in 7 months) is stamped 27 January but describes the week to 28 January; used only for direction because the event precedes the cutoff.
Meme-stock and retail-attention items (n0820 AMC call buying, n0457, n0512, n1689, DWAC moves) were left to the separate retail writer to keep merged citation counts within four.
